title: Leadership
description: These statements explore initiative, decision-making, listening, leading by example and public speaking. They mix beliefs with reported behaviours, so agreement is not a measure of leadership ability.
tip: Choose one small task to take responsibility for, clarify your role with the group and ask for feedback. Practise listening and summarising another person’s view before responding.

questions.text: I take responsibility even when a task is not assigned to me.
I can make tough decisions even if some people disagree with me.
I believe a good leader listens more than they speak.
I prefer to lead by example rather than by giving orders.
I am comfortable speaking in front of a large group.

title: Stress & Problem Solving
description: These statements explore how you describe handling pressure, deadlines, asking for help and responding to setbacks. The responses do not measure stress severity or mental health.
tip: When deadlines overlap, list the next action for each task, clarify priorities and ask for specific help where needed. After a setback, identify one useful lesson without requiring yourself to recover immediately.

questions.text: I stay calm and think clearly under pressure.
I see problems as opportunities to learn, not as setbacks.
I can manage multiple deadlines without panicking.
I ask for help when I feel overwhelmed instead of hiding it.
I bounce back quickly after failure or criticism.

title: Teamwork & Relationships
description: These statements explore cooperation, shared credit, conflict, inclusion and trust. Agreement describes your perspective; it does not establish how others experience working with you.
tip: In your next group task, invite a quieter person’s view, acknowledge specific contributions and restate the shared goal when opinions differ.

questions.text: I find it easy to work with people who have different opinions than me.
I give credit to the team instead of taking it all myself.
I can handle conflict and try to find a solution, not take sides.
I make sure everyone in a group feels included and heard.
I believe trust is more important than being the smartest person in the room.
